Name: Celltainer Biosolutions GmbH
Description:
Celltainer Biosolutions GmbH is the daughter company and responsible for the single-use product line of Bionet, from Spain. Based in Berlin (Germany). The platform is currently used to produce tailored enzyme solutions for agro-industrial side stream valorisation, as well as functional proteins for applications in food, feed, and industry. Name: Plastilose
Description:
We're growing a future without plastic waste.

At Plastilose, we believe the most powerful material of the next century isn't made in a factory. It's grown by bacteria.

We're a Dutch bio-tech company building a new generation of bio-based materials that replace single-use plastics, starting in healthcare. Our first product is a 30ml medicine cup made from bacterial cellulose which is home compostable, free of PFAS and microplastics and fit for hospital use. 

It's already on its way towards a very first hospital through our first pilot with more Dutch hospitals close behind.

But the cup is just the beginning.

What we're really building is a platform for biofabrication. Bacteria that grow strong, versatile materials in days, not centuries. A licensing model that lets factories around the world produce locally instead of shipping plastic across oceans. 

A way to design materials that disappear back into the soil when their job is done.

This work needs builders. Scientists who get excited about fermentation curves. Engineers who want to design a factory from a blank page. Designers who care as much about a hospital nurse's morning routine as they do about climate impact. Operators who can run with ambiguity and make things real.

Today we're a team of eight, based at the Biotech Campus Delft, with a seed round in motion and a roadmap that goes far beyond medicine cups. We work in the lab, on the production floor and in conversations with hospitals, regulators, and investors who want healthcare that doesn't cost the planet.

If you've ever looked at a plastic disposable and thought "there has to be a better way," we'd like to meet you.

We're hiring across bioprocess, robotics automation, product engineering and operations. Open roles live on our careers page, but if you don't see your role listed and you think you'd fit, write to us anyway.

The future of disposables is grown, not made.

See you soon.

Name: Lignitec
Description:
What we do

Lignitec is dedicated to advancing biobased materials that can serve as eco-friendly alternatives to conventional fiberboards like MDF, triplex, OSB, and high-pressure laminate. These traditional materials frequently rely on chemical adhesives and find extensive use in the furniture and construction sectors.
Materials bonded with such adhesives pose a threat to both human health and the environment due to their carcinogenic properties. These materials persistently release these harmful chemicals throughout their entire lifecycle, contributing to unhealthy indoor environments.

Towards the end of their lifecycle, these materials become challenging to recycle due to the presence of these adhesives, leaving us with few options aside from landfill disposal or incineration.

At Lignitec, we believe in the existence of smarter alternatives that are entirely biobased, enabling us to repurpose waste materials from the furniture and construction industries, thereby reducing CO2 emissions and offering a healthy, sustainable substitute for more traditional materials.renewable sources and offers great potential. We are fully dedicated to making a meaningful impact on building a more sustainable and intelligent economy and built environment.

Name: COGEM - Commissie Genetische Modificatie
Description:
The Netherlands Commission on Genetic Modification (COGEM) is an independent scientific advisory committee composed of scientists and experts. The main functions of COGEM are to give statutory advice to the Dutch Minister of Environment on the risks to human health and the environment from experiments under contained conditions (laboratories, greenhouse, production facilities) with Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs), and the release and marketing of GMOs, and to inform the Dutch government of ethical and societal issues linked to genetic modification.

The scope of COGEM covers all fields, ranging from agriculture to medicine and from contained use to deliberate release of GMOs. However, COGEM solely advises on environmental risks and does not advise on food safety, animal welfare, or patient safety (e.g. in relation to gene therapy).

The tasks and structure of COGEM are laid down in the Environmental Protection Act.

Name: Continuous Downstream Processing of Biologics -CODOBIO MSCA ITN
Description:
The main objective of the CODOBIO proposal is to deliver a new generation of creative, entrepreneurial, highly-skilled and innovative Early Stage Researchers (ESRs) that are able to face the future transition challenges and to greatly contribute to the knowledge-based economy and digitized environment in manufacturing and society in general. In the proposed research programme, the most urgent questions in continuous downstream processing will be addressed:

*Process control and modelling of continuous downstream processes
*Miniaturization, scale-up and scale-down of continuous downstream processes
*Process design and development of integrated continuous downstream processes

Furthermore, regulatory framework questions, such as comparability of product quality between batch-wise and continuously manufactured products, will be examined. To achieve project objectives, several disciplines, such as process control, statistical modelling, high end protein analytics and process engineering will be combined following the common goal of continuous manufacturing of biologics. By adding the regulatory and environmental aspects to the scientific, technological and economic approach, we will make our programme interdisciplinary, comprehensive and unique.

Name: Peregrion
Description:
Peregrion is a specialized CRO that supports the acceleration and de-risking of drug development programs. We help pharma companies to collect human Mass Balance and Bioavailability data as early as Phase 1/2a, using our advanced Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (AMS) technology.
Founded as a spin-off of TNO, a leading research institute, Peregrion builds on 10+yrs of AMS innovation. Our mission is to drive faster, safer, and future-oriented clinical development by delivering early human ADME insights. 
Trusted by multiple top 20 pharmaceutical companies, our technology uses at least 100-fold lower radioactivity and delivers at least 500-fold higher analytical sensitivity than conventional methods. This means ultra-low dosing is sufficient. Studies can be added in Phase 1/2a of clinical development, saving up to 2 years in development time.

What this means for your program:
Having the data early in development has multiple benefits, for instance, DDI and impairment studies can be designed using human data; animal metabolism and IV toxicity studies can be waived; studies can be done as an add-on to existing studies (extra cohort); etc.

Peregrion is your trusted go-to partner for the following studies: Mass Balance, Metabolite Profiling, Metabolite Identification, Absolute Bioavailability.
•Mass Balance: Insight into the absorption, metabolism, and excretion of drugs
•Metabolite Profiling: Identifying and quantifying metabolites to understand the metabolism of a drug
•Metabolite Identification: Elucidating the structure of unknown metabolites to evaluate drug safety and efficacy
•Absolute Bioavailability: Fraction of a dose that reaches the systemic circulation unchanged

Microtracer studies are our core business. We are experts in data analysis and interpretation. Using our experience we can support decisions on sample profiling, position of radiolabel, dosing and formulation, bioanalytical methods etc. We work as an extended team member for your team.

Name: InnoFluidics
Description:
InnoFluidics builds the foundation of Agentic BioprocessingTM.
Our label-free, multi-frequency impedance platform characterises the intracellular state of individual cells in real time – directly from suspension, without staining, fixation, or sample preparation. The physics is grounded in Maxwell-Wagner dielectric theory, not statistical correlation.
Every decision upstream – clone selection, media and feed optimisation, metabolic shift detection, harvest timing, scale-up comparability – depends on cell state. Yet today's bioprocess analytical stack reads the medium, not the cell. The intracellular biology is inferred, not measured. We close that gap at the measurement physics, then build the intelligence architecture above it.
Three layers sit on top of the hardware: perception (Coupled Dispersion Analytics), cognition (Biological Behaviour Interpretation), and federated memory (Federated Biological Knowledge). Together they turn direct intracellular measurement into real-time biological reasoning that the process itself can act on – progressing from deterministic look-up tables to shadow-mode validation to supervised autonomous control.
InnoFluidics is not an AI company that needs data. It is not a sensor company that needs algorithms. The complete  architecture – from the measurement physics to the fleet knowledge repository – is proprietary and patent-protected.
The technology is built on roughly 20 years of research. The instrument is deployable in bioprocess labs today. Revenue to date comes from early pharma engagements, including repeat business with GSK.
We are currently onboarding a limited group of pharma, biotech, and CDMO partners who will co-shape the roadmap from real-time intracellular measurement to autonomous bioprocess control.
Headquartered in Eindhoven (Netherlands), with a sister entity, InnoFluidics Diagnostics, in Diepenbeek (Belgium).

Name: iGEM Groningen 2023
Description:
The International Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) competition is a prestigious synthetic biology competition. Each year, 350 worldwide university teams compete to design the most innovative biological system. We are the team representing the University of Groningen in 2023.

Our team (bye-o-film) focuses on the problem of biofilm formation on medical devices. Biofilms, which are collections of bacteria held together by a matrix of extracellular substances, are difficult to treat with traditional methods like antibiotics. They are highly resistant to antimicrobial agents and can develop further resistance through the exchange of genes. Biofilm formation on implants is of particular interest due to the increasing number of medical procedures involving such devices, such as joint replacement surgery.

We intend to develop an innovative approach to offer alternative treatments for biofilms while helping medical specialists monitor the status of devices post-intervention. This solution involves engineering an E. coli-based biosensor that detects biofilm formation and releases bacteriophages, which can disrupt the biofilm. The biosensor uses an M13 helper phage to create an amplified signal upon sensing biofilm formation through quorum-sensing molecules. The M13 phage also contains a matrix-degrading enzyme to disrupt biofilm formation, making the infection more manageable with antibiotics. The biosensor system is designed to send a signal that is interpreted by an electronic device. The final component is an interface that communicates these actions to patients and medical specialists, providing early indication of biofilm formation with an app.

We envision designing this system as a modular toolkit for detecting and eliminating various types of biofilms. Our goal is to provide a useful tool for both medical professionals and the general public.

Name: CIRCLE Project
Description:
To be competitive and to ensure sustainability in the face of global challenges and technological advancements, the European industrial sector must urgently introduce drastic changes to comply with net-zero targets, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and to shift towards an environmentally, economically, and socially sustainable development. Highly efficient and cost-effective biorefinery systems are recognised as solid solutions that support our industrial transition towards this direction. Nonetheless, it remains a crucial challenge to achieve a sustainable model for their adequate implementation. The chemical industry in Europe is a crucial driver of the economy; however, it faces several challenges, such as greenhouse gas emissions, high energy costs, and dependence on foreign sources due to its reliance on fossil resources. While the bioeconomy is an essential strategy to address these challenges, there is a significant gap between the consumption and domestic production of bio-based platform chemicals in Europe.

To tackle this issue, the CIRCLE consortium is working on an innovative retrofitted biorefinery. This biorefinery will transform food waste streams and other biomasses into high-value bio-based chemicals and intermediates such as lactic acid (LA) and its derived products, including polylactic acid (PLA)-based ones. The project aims to upgrade the capacity of an existing biogas plant and contribute to the production of bio-based chemicals in Europe by valorising food waste streams.

Our specialists are capable of customizing the functionalities (e.g., degradation and viscosity) of these forms by influencing the chemical interaction between the individual biopolymer chains. BioMed Elements can influence the functional properties (e.g., absorption, pliability) of the matter by tuning the particle characteristics. 

BioMed Elements gives their customers access to natural materials, but with the added control over functionality and specifications. This unique combination makes these natural materials useful for many more applications. The team, based in TU/e, is comprised of talented and motivated students from a variety of disciplines, including medical sciences, applied physics, computer science and biomedical engineering. Together, we are working hard to develop a biosensor that can accurately and efficiently detect creatinine continuously.

We consider our work incredibly important, as kidney failure is a significant health concern around the world. By developing a biosensor that can detect creatinine, healthcare providers could quickly and easily monitor the development of kidney failure and start dialysis on time. 

We will present our biosensor at the SensUs 2025 competition at the end of August 2025, together with other student teams from all over the world working on the same goal.

To successfully create and scale a novel bioprocess, you need to start with the end in mind: what technical performance do you need from your strain, substrate, and equipment to allow you to sell your product at a competitive price in the long run? What does your facility need to look like to extract maximum performance out of your microorganism? Or, the other way around, what should your microorganism look like to optimally fit your facility?

At Formical, we provide a bioprocess data platform to help accelerate biotech R&D using three pillars:
- Automation: to free up cognitive space and speed up iteration
- Integration: to connect silos in data, processes, and teams
- Virtualization: to ‘fail fast’ and prevent expensive physical mistakes

Using our platform you create a unified overview of both upstream and downstream bioprocessing. We can connect Formical to all equipment to automate data collection and integration, to save 8-25 hours per week per engineer in manual data processing. Audion's mission is to improve the lives of patients suffering from the most prevalent forms of hearing. In 2015, almost 7% of the world’s population, approximately half a billion people, had disabling hearing loss. In 2015 hearing loss was the 4th leading cause of years lived with disability (YLDs). The reach of hearing loss extends far beyond sensory impairment in young as well as older people and is associated with increase in dementia.  Yet no drug treatments currently exist. Audion is committed to discovering effective therapies through our world-leading research into inner ear cellular biology and physiology.

LY3056480 is a potent small molecule gamma-secretase inhibitor identified by Audion and Eli Lilly scientists. Preclinical development was completed in 2017 and a phase 1 study has been completed in which the drug has been shown to be safe upon transtympanic administration. A phase 2 study has been finished and long term followup data analysed in 2021, with promising signs of efficacy.

To develop LY3056480 we collaborate with leading research institutions and companies both in the EU and US and are currently interested in partnerships with pharmaceutical companies committed to bringing treatments for sensorineural hearing loss to market.

Name: GENIE
Description:
Developing a functional secondary diagnostic tool that serves to identify non-coding gene variants and their influence on pathogenic gene expression.

Rare diseases affect 3-5% of the global populace, although a seemingly negligible statistic, this translates to circa 300 million people. While the majority of research for genetically-linked diseases is conducted with a focus on coding regions, new evidence highlights the pivotal contribution of functional genetic variants in non-coding regions to disease pathology. Given the potential effects exerted on neighboring functional genes, non-coding genes may act as regulatory elements modulating gene expression and genome structure. To investigate these relationships, we will be leveraging WGS (whole genome sequencing) technologies, considering their ability to characterize non-coding variants. Despite these objectives, intron-contingent disease pathology remains under-researched and underrepresented in current models, and we aim to contribute to the expansion of intron-regulated diagnostic research through the development of an annotation-based machine learning model.

Het mogelijk maken voor iedereen om puur en pesticidenvrij te eten, met een oplossing die werkt en vertrouwen geeft.

He has a clear vision that the connection between R&D and business is essential for successful valorization and is dedicated to collaborate with clients to support them in making these connections. 
Together, let’s drive innovation forward!

Name: Dutch Life Sciences conference
Description:
Dutch Life Sciences conference is Netherlands ́ most established life sciences event. It has positioned itself as the premier annual meeting place for both Dutch and international players. The event brings together leading CEOs of biotech, pharma and medical devices companies, heads of R&D, academics, and life sciences investors from the healthcare sector for networking opportunities to promote the translation of inventions into e.g. therapies, medical devices and diagnostics distribution in and across the healthcare system. It provides a unique opportunity for discussions, panel presentations and product demonstrations and to meet new companies, paving the way for new business collaborations. 

The conference will discuss 8 main topics, to be announced. Our esteemed speakers and thought leaders will explore the latest trends, cutting-edge technologies and disruptive business strategies that are reshaping the life sciences landscape. 

Together, let ́s unlock the full potential of scaling up, shaping a healthier and more sustainable future for all.

The 20th edition of the Dutch Life Sciences conference will take place on December 12th 2024.

Check out the complete programme for all the topics that will be addressed. In addition the winner of the Venture Challenge Fall will be announced.

Name: NBCL
Description: NBCL has developed a point of care analyzer with a five-minute whole blood intact PTH assay that can be operated by anyone.

Name: QVQ Holding BV
Description:
We provide our clients a one-stop shop for lead panel antibody discovery.
This service include llama immunization (in collaboration), construction of phage display libraries, custom-tailored selection procedures, production of VHH, plain or equipped with different tags in bacteria and yeast.

We have developed single-domain antibodies that are well characterized and can assist you in your research. They are all available with a free cysteine for directional labeling with biotin, fluorescent labels or chelators.

Name: VivArt-X
Description:
VivArt-X is a medical technology spin-off from Eindhoven University of Technology, dedicated to developing advanced biomaterials for personalized regenerative solutions.
Our mission is to redefine the standard of care in breast reconstruction: enabling predictable restoration, reconstruction, and regeneration of breast tissue with lasting results. Founded in 2022, VivArt-X has already gained broad recognition and multiple awards for its mission to restore confidence and redefine possibilities in regenerative medicine.

Name: Biolegio
Description:
For more than two decades, Biolegio has been a pioneer in the
custom synthesis of oligonucleotides, empowering researchers
worldwide to advance the fields of life science and molecular
diagnostics.

Together, let us embark on a mission to push scientific progress and
innovation worldwide. We are eager to collaborate with you as your
trusted oligo supply partner.

Name: Clinichain B.V.
Description:
Welcome to Clinichain, your global partner for tailor-made clinical trial equipment solutions. 

At Clinichain, we are dedicated to enhancing global healthcare by fostering transparency, flexibility, and maintaining high-quality standards in clinical trials.

We specialize in providing timely delivery of clinical equipment and connected devices to support logistic needs for both global decentralized and traditional studies. Our tailored rental/purchase solutions are designed to adapt to your clinical trial phase, geographic complexities, and allow flexibility, ensuring seamless drug development processes.

With a presence in over 150 countries and a robust network of global agents and brokers, Clinichain ensures that medical equipment and any type of devices are delivered on-site, precisely when needed, anywhere in the world.

Our sourcing solutions cater to both standard and specific clinical equipment needs, offering comprehensive support throughout the trial process. We prioritize efficiency, compliance, and a dedication to improving global healthcare outcomes through innovative solutions in clinical trials.

Clinichain leads the way in facilitating clinical trials, streamlining access to medical equipment and logistical support. Join us in revolutionizing the landscape of healthcare research and development, one trial at a time.
